messages.subject: heteroscedasticity and prediction
parts:
Hi all, 
I've a model with heteroscedasticity in a factor with 7 levels. Following the description found on the discussion forum and in the help files I modeled this with an extra 7 columns as the Y variable with the data on the right place. Basically something like:

           X1        X2        X3        X4        X5        X6        X7    Y         spec Side

5   -17.61400        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA 2011       Agelas E-NE
6   -18.16500        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA 2011       Agelas E-NE
7   -18.01700        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA 2011       Agelas E-NE
8          NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA -19.83800 2011 Xestospongia S-SE
9          NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA -19.71200 2011 Xestospongia S-SE
10         NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA -21.24300 2011 Xestospongia E-NE
11         NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA -19.50600 2011 Xestospongia E-NE
12         NA        NA        NA        NA        NA        NA -19.25400 2011 Xestospongia E-
...

This worked perfectly!

Now I want to use the predict to visualize the model which has an interaction. 
I know one can do this by including NA rows (for the Y variables) and the control.predictor, but I can't get this to work. 
For example:
adding 28 lines
NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 2011       Agelas E-NE
NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 2013       Agelas E-NE
...
after the data.

I always get the following error message:
Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE,  : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 148, 120
Apparently, adding the extra rows (with only NAs for the first 7 columns) makes the program not recognize that it now needs to make predictions for the extra 28 lines.

The other method to create prediction, using lincomb, actually worked, but my question is why didn't my first attempt work?
Any suggestions?
Thanks for your attention.
cheers, Erik

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] heteroscedasticity and prediction
parts:
I am not sure I understood you correctly, but:

When doing predictions you cannot add rows of only NA. You should add "normal rows" where the observed y-value is NA.

The covariate values used in your "fake data rows" should be like the values used in the lincombs.

Kind regards,
Haakon
